case_title.quote: NARENDER SINGH & ORS. v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH

number_of_accused.quote: A2 toA6 are the appellants before us in these two appeals.
number_of_accused.reason: Five appellants (A2 to A6) are decided.

accused_gender.quote: A5 while abusing the deceased and making a pronouncement that he cannot escape that day
accused_gender.reason: The judgment refers to the accused as 'he' and 'accused' persons; A5 is male, so gender is stated.

accused_caste.correct_value: Same community (unnamed) as each other; caste not named
accused_caste.quote: the appellants who all belonged to same community
accused_caste.reason: The judgment mentions a common community but does not name it.

victim_gender.reason: The victim is male (Ram Bhuvan, son of Sunder Lal Sharma).

accused_victim_relationship.quote: due to old enmity, attacked with sharp weapon with intention to kill
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Old enmity is recorded; the value qualifies it properly. The warning not to contest elections also suggests rivalry.

offence_category.quote: convicted the appellants accused for the offence under Section 302

statutory_provisions.reason: Charges and conviction are accurately given.

weapon.quote: A5 was holding a sword, A6 was holding a Farsa, A2 was having an axe while A1, A3 and A4 were having lathis

evidence_type.quote: supported by medical evidence as well
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical, documentary and recovery evidence are all reflected.

confession.quote: Section 27 Statement under Exhibits P18 to P21
confession.reason: Section 27 statements are mentioned, with no confession.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: attacked with sharp weapon with intention to kill

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted the appellants accused for the offence under Section 302 read with Sections 148 and 149 IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: The Division Bench having confirmed the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants
high_court_outcome.reason: The High Court appeal was dismissed and the conviction confirmed.

offence_finally_established.quote: Section 302 read with Sections 148 and 149 IPC

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove 'sarpanch' reference only if needed; otherwise remove 'The accused were arrested...' is fine; main problem: 'The express report was received... ' is fine. Revise to avoid 'a village sarpanch' no issue; remove 'Several men' claim of 'the rest lathis' is fine.
neutral_facts.quote: The deceased was the Sarpanch of the village
neutral_facts.reason: It is largely accurate and has no outcome leak. It states the shifting of the body 'by 7:30 a.m.' as hospital time, and calls it 'Witnesses who came on hearing shouts'. These are minor.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the punishment prescribed.

attempt_completion.reason: The deceased died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.quote: as many as 8 injuries were noted on the body of the deceased
physical_harm.reason: Death with 8 injuries, 4 grievous; P.W.3 was also injured.

number_of_offences.quote: convicted the appellants accused for the offence under Section 302 read with Sections 148 and 149 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Five sections charged is right, but the count of three upheld is debatable; conviction is under s.302 r/w ss.148/149.

motive.reason: Alleged motive is properly marked as such.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: his evidence fully supported the case of the prosecution

witness_credibility.quote: evidence of P.W.3 as an eye witness was cogent in every respect

post_offence_conduct.quote: left the place of occurrence along with other accused
post_offence_conduct.reason: Matches; the arrest and recoveries are also reflected.

trial_duration.reason: The dates match and the trial judgment date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: Tripurari Ray, Dhirendra Singh Parmar... Arjun Garg, Manish Yadav, Mishra Saurabh

procedural_irregularity.quote: such a delay has not caused any serious prejudice to the appellants

appeal_history.quote: The Division Bench having confirmed the conviction and sentence

prosecution_argument.quote: the arrest of the accused and the seizure made by the panch witnesses duly established

defence_argument.quote: the FIR was ante-dated and that the appellants were falsely implicated

legal_principle_applied.quote: Every such delay is not fatal unless prejudice to the accused is shown.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Pala Singh v. State of Punjab (1972) 2 SCC 640
precedent_relied_upon.reason: The three cases are correctly cited.
